targetWords.definition: An addict is a person who cannot stop doing or having something.
targetWords.example: She was a coffee addict. She had more than three cups each day.

targetWords.definition: When something is archeological, it relates to archeology.
targetWords.example: They found archeological evidence that proved an ancient species of man.

targetWords.definition: Archeology is the study of ancient people through their artifacts.
targetWords.example: He studied archeology to learn more about ancient Egyptian culture.

targetWords.definition: To brainstorm is to have a lot of ideas about a certain topic.
targetWords.example: ■ The students met after school to brainstorm ideas for their assignment. budget [bAd3 it] n.

targetWords.definition: —►His budget for food was very tight.
targetWords.example: His budget for food was very tight.

targetWords.definition: When something is chaotic, it is crazy, confused, and hectic.
targetWords.example: The first day of school can be chaotic for a new student.

targetWords.definition: To cite something is to mention it as an example or as proof of something.
targetWords.example: She cited six reasons that the school needed to build new classrooms.

targetWords.definition: To correspond is to match or to be similar to something.
targetWords.example: The boy's story didn't correspond with his mother's version. courtyard [kortjaxd] n.

targetWords.definition: - » During the summer, the courtyard is a nice place to have lunch.
An estate is a large area of land owned by a family or organization.
targetWords.example: He lived on his father's estate in the country.

targetWords.definition: Fraud is the crime of gaining money by lying or by tricking people.
targetWords.example: Experts say that credit card fraud increases around the holidays.

targetWords.definition: Hydrogen is a gas that has no taste, color, or smell.
targetWords.example: Balloons filled with hydrogen can easily float away if you aren't careful.

targetWords.definition: Integrity is honesty and good morals.
targetWords.example: The principal had a lot of integrity.

targetWords.definition: To knit is to make fabric by connecting strings together.
targetWords.example: My grandmother knitted me a sweater.

targetWords.definition: An outlook is a person's opinion or way of thinking about something.
targetWords.example: He changed his outlook about rats after he read a book about them. parachute [paeraju:t] n.

targetWords.definition: —► They used parachutes dropped from airplanes to send supplies to the civilians.
targetWords.example: They used parachutes dropped from airplanes to send supplies to the civilians.

targetWords.definition: When something is prehistoric, it is from a time when there was no written history.
targetWords.example: The scientists found prehistoric pots used by the people in the area. proponent [prapounant] n.

targetWords.definition: —*He was a proponent of using environmentally friendly products.
targetWords.example: He was a proponent of using environmentally friendly products.

targetWords.definition: To refine something is to make it better by making changes.
targetWords.example: The principal refined his method of controlling students over the years.

targetWords.definition: To restrict is to limit something and prevent it from getting bigger.
targetWords.example: The club restricted the amount of members.

story.title: The History of Parachutes
story.passage:
Scientists who study archeology say that there may be some evidence of prehistoric

parachutes. But the first written history of the device comes from China about 2,100

years ago. Scientists cite an ancient book that describes parachutes. However, there is no

archeological evidence that proves that an actual parachute was ever made. Later, people

from northern Africa and Italy also had ideas about a similar invention. In fact, a Leonardo

Da Vinci's drawing corresponds closely with the modern parachute design!

In 1783, French scientist Sebastian Lenormand invented the first modern parachute.

Sebastian brainstormed with other scientists to come up with a way to help people jump

safely out of burning buildings. He thought the solution was to give people an object to

restrict their speed while they traveled toward the ground. Many people thought that he

was up to some kind of fraud, but Sebastian had a lot of integrity. His budget was limited,

so he first tested his theory by using two umbrellas. He jumped
